content: The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA) were represented by Deborah Yokoe in efforts related to infection prevention and control. The World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Offices were represented by Lucia Alonso (Americas), Deborah Barassa and Landry Cihambanya (Africa), Ana Paula Coutinho Rehse (Europe), Pilar Ramon-Pardo (Americas), Aparna Shah (South-East Asia), and Li Zhao (Western Pacific). At WHO headquarters, the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) teams, under the Country Readiness Strengthening and WHO Health Emergencies Programme (WHE), included contributors such as Devika Dixit, Kathleen Dunn, Hannah Hamilton, Hibak Osman Mahamed, Brenda Caceres Mejia, Maria Clara Padoveze, Nosheen Usman, and Victoria Willet. João Paulo Toledo contributed from the IPC Unit, IPC Taskforce, and the Global IPC Network. The Emergency Event Response Unit, under Strategic Health Operations (WHE), included Ana Hoxha and Boris Pavlin. The High Impact Epidemics Unit, under Health Emergency Interventions (WHE), included Pierre Formenty and Anaïs Legand. It was developed through consultations with member states, including representatives from the Ministries of Health and Agriculture of Iran, Oman, the Russian Federation, and Türkiye, as well as experts from WHO, the CDC, and specialists in infectious diseases, laboratory sciences, and vector control. These experts participated as WHO Temporary Advisers and declared no conflicts of interest. The recommendations for transmission-based precautions specific to CCHF were developed during a consultation meeting in Muscat, Oman, in December 2015, and were published in a 2016 summary report. Additional evidence is needed in areas such as aerosol transmission risks outside of medical procedures, criteria for discontinuing isolation, and refining healthcare-associated infection (HAI) case definitions for CCHF. Future revisions of the guidance will incorporate new evidence as it becomes available. The document underwent review by the IPC Public Health Emergencies Working Group and WHO regional IPC focal points, with feedback integrated into the final version. External reviewers also completed conflict-of-interest declarations, and no conflicts were identified. For further details on authorship and contributions, refer to the acknowledgment section. The operational guide is available in both electronic and print formats, with publication rights reserved by WHO.
